title: Reinforce preemptive fairness for latency-sensitive batches to prevent request starvation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalations from multiple tenants (hosted + Dedicated) reported recurring P99 tail spikes and timeouts for low-token, latency-sensitive requests during sustained high-volume long-context streaming traffic. Investigation showed the continuous-batching scheduler's backpressure and batching heuristics allowed large-context flows to accumulate in the active queue and monopolize batch formation, starving short requests and causing long-context tail latency amplification and client timeouts.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in prod-sim using tenant traffic mix (long-streaming + small chat) — P99 for small flows rose from baseline 0.9s to 3.2s under a sustained 30% long-context load.
- Scheduler queue snapshot (2025-11-05 incident) showed >70% of active batch tokens were held by 8 inflight large-context requests.
- Root cause: batch scoring used raw token count without per-flow aging or soft-priority lanes; backpressure only triggered when queue exceeded absolute token capacity, allowing transient monopolization.
- Edge case exacerbated on Dedicated where pinned GPU pools had fewer concurrent batch slots and on Private installs with conservative autoscaler settings.
- Also discovered a priority inversion: aged small requests waited behind large requests with older start times because token-based batching favored larger effective batch utility metric.
root_cause: Scheduler batch utility metric weighted absolute token contribution without accounting for per-request latency sensitivity or request age. Backpressure thresholds were absolute and coarse, enabling large-context floods to form oversized batches that delayed small requests. On Dedicated/Private, limited batch slots and conservative pooling amplified the effect.
fix_summary:
Implemented 'soft-priority lanes' and preemptive fairness:
1) Introduced a latency-sensitive lane that tags requests with short target tail latency (heuristic + explicit header).
2) Modified batch scoring to include request age and latency-sensitivity weight, decaying the advantage of large-context requests over time.
3) Added per-flow max-hold-time (soft preemption) to force batch commit when a high-priority request would otherwise be delayed beyond SLO.
4) Tuned backpressure to use relative token percentiles instead of absolute thresholds and added per-pool safeguards for Dedicated/Private.
5) Added a configurable kill-switch and telemetry flags to rollback per-tenant if regressions observed.
test_results: Canary (alpha tenants): small-flow P99 improved from 3.2s -> 0.9s; overall token throughput dropped 2.1% (within SLAs). Dedicated internal cluster stress test: reduced long-context tail variance by 48%. Regression suite added: 12 new tests covering aging, preemption, lane demotion, and Dedicated pool limits.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy scheduler changes to staging and run tenant-mix load tests (24h).
2) Canary rollout to 5 low-risk hosted tenants + 2 Dedicated customers (configurable flag). Monitor latency P50/P99, batch formation size, dropped/aborted batches.
3) Incrementally enable for remaining hosted tenants and Dedicated pools over 72h.
4) Offer Private customers a patch bundle with upgrade guide and toggle for soft-priority behavior.
5) Full rollout target: runtime-1.23 GA after 2-week canary with no critical regressions.
notes_on_private_deployments: Private/on-prem customers often run older autoscaler configs; patch provides configuration flags and a checklist to ensure pool_size and max_concurrent_batches are set to recommended values. Ship both RPM and container images; include an offline upgrade path for air-gapped installs.
